executionPlan: Wrote the shell regression test first and proved it red, then fixed the stale strip flag, eased the exit fov to a zero-velocity arrival, traced the uncaught rejection to the drei meshopt decoder and disabled it, and split failure messages into plain text plus developer detail; verified on the production build with the real-GPU headless Chrome.
actualModel: claude-sonnet-5-5 (unverified; field normalized by the Boss)
summary: All four QA findings are fixed. The regression test was red on the old code and is green now. In a production build, the focus probes, failure paths, exit traces and cycles all check out. Lint, tests and build exit 0. Nothing is committed.

testsRun.command: npm run build (copy of the tree)

criteria.criterion: F-M2-1 is fixed: after any Play in which the inline strip was shown (slow load past 400 ms, touch device code-only prefetch, or Retry after a failure), Exit never mounts the strip and focus ends on Play; a shell test that shows the strip, enters, exits and asserts the active element is Play fails on the current code and passes after the fix, and QA's focus probe (focusin and focusout log around Exit) shows Play as the only focus target in the browser for the slow-load and mobile-emulation cases.
criteria.evidence: Root cause as QA found it: swap() called stripOut() but left stripShownAt set. The fix resets stripShownAt in swap() after stripOut(). I also made LoadingStrip focus Cancel on mount only when visible, as defense in depth. Regression tests in shell.test.tsx: the harness now renders the real LoadingStrip, and the two Exit tests (slow load, Retry then Exit) assert the strip stays off and Play has focus. A third test covers a strip that mounts faded out. Before the fix: 3 failed of 44 (red-before-fix.txt). After the fix: 44 of 44 pass. Browser (production build), probes stalestrip.mjs 900 ms, mfocus.mjs mobile and desktop, mfocus2 and mfocus3: strip shown during load = true, strip seen during Exit = false. The log after Exit shows only the Exit button losing focus, then Play gaining it. Final active element is BUTTON play / explore in every run. Output files: stalestrip.txt, mfocus-mobile.txt, mfocus-desktop.txt, mfocus2.txt, mfocus3.txt.

criteria.criterion: F-M2-3 and F-M2-4 are fixed: no uncaught promise rejection is logged for any failure path (WebAssembly rejected, chunk blocked, clips blocked, context lost), and the failure dialog shows a plain-language sentence with no chunk number or URL while the technical detail stays available to developers (console or a details element).
criteria.evidence: F-M2-3 cause: the 'Uncaught (in promise)' was not in the physics chunk. It came from drei useGLTF creating the three-stdlib MeshoptDecoder, which starts an un-awaited WebAssembly.instantiate. The hero Avatar triggered it on page load whenever WebAssembly was blocked. None of our GLBs use meshopt or draco (checked the files). Avatar.tsx (useGLTF and preload calls) and GameAvatar.tsx now pass useMeshOpt=false. Hero-only probe: errors before the fix 'Uncaught (in promise)', after 'none' (heroerr.mjs). Production build, failures-prod.mjs: physics (WebAssembly blocked) has 0 promise rejections. Its only error is React's own console.error 'Error: WebAssembly blocked by the test', the caught-error log from the error boundary, which is not an uncaught rejection. Network (chunks blocked), clips and context-lost show errors 'none' and 0 promise rejections. In dev, React still re-throws the caught Physics error as 'Uncaught Error' (not a promise). That is dev-only and was not present in the production build. F-M2-4: gameLoader.ts failed state now has a plain message per reason (network, physics, timeout) plus a separate detail field. The raw text goes to console.warn only. Production dialog text, network case: 'The game could not be downloaded. Check your connection, then retry, or go back to the portfolio.' Physics: 'The game engine could not start in this browser. Retry, or go back to the portfolio.' New gameLoader test asserts a raw 'Loading chunk 186 failed. (error: http://...)' never reaches message and is kept in detail and the console. Existing loader and shell tests were updated to the plain messages. Output files: prod-physics.txt, prod-network.txt, prod-clips.txt, prod-context.txt, physics-before.txt, physics-after.txt.

assumptions: No physical touch device was used. The mobile case was Chrome emulation with coarse pointer and touch events.
The Exit pixel-exact result and the cycles baseline were compared with QA's recorded numbers. QA's old tree was not re-run side by side.
The meshopt decoder is now off for every useGLTF call. If a future asset is meshopt-compressed, it must opt back in explicitly.

In production the physics failure still logs one console.error from React (the error boundary's caught-error log). This is not an uncaught rejection. Monitoring that counts console.error would still see it.
The one pre-existing lint warning in useRealtimeChat.ts is unfixed because that file is outside this stage.
The failure-path probes block WebAssembly entirely, a synthetic condition. Real-device and real-network behaviour was not tested.
decisionsProposed: Disable the meshopt decoder (useGLTF useMeshOpt false) for every GLB load including the hero, because no asset uses meshopt and its default un-awaited WebAssembly instantiate logs an uncaught rejection.
lessonsProposed: A shell test harness must render the real child components that have mount side effects (focus, timers). A hook-only harness hid the F-M2-1 focus theft.
Fix 'uncaught rejection' reports by finding the real origin first. Here a drei default (the meshopt decoder) in the hero caused it, not the physics chunk the stack seemed to point to.
When an exit tween ends with zero velocity, a pixel-diff metric around the swap is dominated by the chrome fade-in. Judge landing smoothness from fov and silhouette-height traces instead.
